transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Well, I'm here because I've been having this issue with eating. I work as a cashier, and after my shifts, I just keep buying these huge takeout orders. I mean, it's like enough food for a whole family—burgers, fries, chicken, a bunch of desserts. And I'll just sit there and eat almost all of it by myself before I even go home.
During these eating episodes after work, do you feel like you're unable to stop eating, even if you wanted to?

Yeah, that's exactly it. Once I take that first bite, it just feels like something in me clicks off. Even while I’m sitting there telling myself, 'Demetrius, stop, you don’t need any more,' my hands just keep reaching for the next thing. I just can't seem to make myself stop.
After you finish eating all that food, do you do anything to try to counteract it—like making yourself vomit, taking laxatives, exercising excessively, or fasting the next day?

No, I don't do any of that. I don't make myself throw up or take pills or anything like that. And I definitely don't exercise like crazy. Honestly, after I eat all of it, I just feel so stuffed and heavy... I usually just go home and lay down. I don't starve myself the next day either, if that's what you mean. I just kind of wake up and go about my normal day, even though I feel terrible about what I did the night before.
How often would you say these episodes of eating large amounts of food happen? Is it every day, several times a week, once a week, or less often than that?

It's pretty often. For the last several months, it’s been happening... I'd say three or four nights most weeks. And honestly, I can’t remember a single week where I didn’t do it at least once. At least not since the foreclosure calls started coming in.

When you're about to start eating all that food, or while you're eating, what are you feeling emotionally? Are you stressed, anxious, upset about something—or does it feel more like you're just physically hungry?

Honestly, most of the time I'm not even hungry when it starts. It's definitely not physical hunger. Like, I might have already eaten a full dinner with my wife, but I still end up looking for more food. It's more about... I guess I'm just trying to shut my head off. With all the stress and the worry about the house, eating just kind of makes my brain stop thinking for a little while.
When you think about these eating episodes and what you're doing, how much does it bother you or upset you? Does it affect your mood, your relationship with your wife, or how you feel about yourself?

It bothers me a lot. I mean, I still get to my cashier shifts and do my job, so I haven't missed work over it, but... it's definitely taking a toll. 

The worst part is that I’m spending money we really don’t have right now just to buy all this extra food. And I'm keeping more and more secrets from my wife about what I'm doing and where the money is going. It just makes being at home feel really tense and... dishonest, I guess. I hate feeling like I'm hiding things from her, but I just don't know how to stop.
Have you noticed changes in your weight over these past several months since these eating episodes have been happening regularly?
I haven't really been paying attention to the scale, to be honest. I mean, my clothes still fit about the same, so I don't think there's been a big change. But I'm not totally sure.

Just to be completely clear—in the time since these eating episodes started a few months ago, have you ever used any diet pills, laxatives, or diuretics to try to control your weight or make up for the eating?
No, I haven't done anything like that. I don't use diet pills or laxatives or anything. I just... eat. I haven't tried to undo it or anything like that.
When you're having these eating episodes or thinking about them afterward, do you feel ashamed, embarrassed, or disgusted with yourself about what you're doing?

Yeah, I do. I feel really ashamed about it. That's... that's why I hide it. I'll pick up food and just sit in my car in the parking lot and eat it all so no one sees me. Or if I'm at home, I'll wait until my wife is completely asleep before I go to the kitchen. And then I make sure to shove all the wrappers, the bags, the receipts... I push them way down deep in the trash can so she won't see how much I actually ate. I'm just too embarrassed for anyone to know.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient meets full diagnostic criteria for Binge Eating Disorder (F50.81). He experiences recurrent episodes of binge eating (3-4 nights per week for several months) characterized by consumption of objectively large amounts of food with a sense of loss of control. Episodes are triggered by emotional distress (foreclosure stress) rather than physical hunger. He demonstrates marked distress, shame, and embarrassment about the behavior, along with functional impairment (financial strain, marital tension, secrecy). The psychosocial stressor (foreclosure) is clearly identified as a precipitant.
